GOLD_Q-15.answer:
oh man, choosing a place to live... it's always this balance between wanting freedom and having some basic stability. i don't want to be tied down but i also need a roof over my head and food on the table.

last time i moved, it was just me and a cat in a car crossing state lines, no job lined up or anything, just an itch for somewhere new. i picked this rainy coastal city mostly because it felt like it would be hard to get bored here, with the ocean and the hills and all these hidden streets. plus it's a little more of an art world than where i was before so that's been great for my work.

in terms of specifics, i look at cost of living vs my freelance income, public transit options (i'm not getting a car anytime soon), access to nature, the vibe of the neighborhoods... and then there's just this weird gut feeling too. like when i walk into an apartment or sit in a coffee shop and it just feels right or wrong, you know? that's a big part of it too.

this city has been good so far, really good. it's taken some time to build up a network and find my way around but it was worth the leap. next time i might consider somewhere with even better art resources, maybe a city that doesn't get quite as much rain... but for now, this is home base and i'm happy here.
